hero.title: Rehearse the Moon and Mars without leaving Earth.
hero.text: Pathfinders42 finds and characterises places on Earth that resemble the landing sites, caves and exploration regions of the Moon and Mars. With NASA open data, and saying where the resemblance fails too.

challenge.title: Artemis is going back to the Moon to stay. Before that, everything is rehearsed on Earth.
challenge.p1: Equipment, rovers and astronauts are tested in places on Earth that resemble their destination. But the known analogues (Atacama, Haughton crater, Death Valley, Mojave) are few and not fully characterised.
challenge.p2: Our question: which other places on the planet work, for what use and to what extent?
challenge.imageAlt: Earth at night seen from space with only six points of light: the known analogues
challenge.caption: The known analogues can be counted on the fingers of one hand.

how.title: Beyond visual resemblance: we compare layer by layer.
how.step1: A landing site, an Artemis region or a cave on the Moon or Mars: from Apollo 11 to Mons Mouton.
how.step2: Topography, climate, geology, ice and caves, measured with physical data from both bodies, against regions all over Earth.
how.step3: Each pair says which layers match, which do not and which limits no place on Earth can reproduce.
how.exampleLabel: Example result, with real data from the API
how.limits: Always fail: reduced gravity, lunar vacuum and radiation.
how.explorerAlt: Screenshot of the Pathfinders42 explorer with the global map of the Moon and the south pole
how.explorerCaption: The explorer: the sites of the Moon and Mars, on the map and in a list.

uses.title: A good analogue for landing is not the same as one for building.
uses.text: Each mission use weighs the layers differently.
uses.landing: Topography matters most: slope and relief.
uses.landingAlt: Lunar ridge lit by a low sun next to a crater in shadow
uses.construction: Geology rules: rock and regolith to use in situ.
uses.constructionAlt: White rock outcrop resembling the anorthosite of the lunar highlands
uses.ice: Ice at the lunar poles against frozen ground on Earth.
uses.iceAlt: Ice polygons in Arctic permafrost seen from the air
uses.caves: Lava tubes and pits as shelter from radiation.
uses.cavesAlt: Inside a lava tube with an opening in the roof letting the light in

mars.title: Only the sky gives away which planet you are on.
mars.text: The Martian sites (landings, exploration regions and caves) are compared with the same rule.
mars.imageAlt: Split landscape: on the left an Earth desert with a blue sky and on the right Mars with an orange sky; the ground is almost identical

ai.title: And an AI looks for the analogues nobody has studied yet.
ai.p1: A machine learning model scans the whole Earth on a fine grid, learns from the known analogues and proposes new candidate regions for each mission use.
ai.p2: The text of each result comes from fixed rules over the measurements: the AI proposes, the data explains.
ai.imageAlt: A rover and two people in suits doing field tests in a volcanic desert

limits.title: What Earth can never imitate.
limits.text: No pair on Earth reproduces these limits. We show them in every result so nobody is misled.
